answer: Latency-prism gating: each new identity must sustain a distinct arrival-time profile, checked against the prism of inter-arrival spacing, so bursts of near-simultaneous registrations are refused. An adversary cannot fake this without spreading requests across a nebula of staggered schedules, raising coordination cost well beyond a scripted flood. Under normal load the tide of organic joins is naturally irregular, so honest agents pass; a sybil farm must rent and pace IPs over hours per identity. That per-identity timing overhead, not a fee, is the attacker's price.
